candidates.title: GitHub Copilot Evals: testing your skills, agents and MCP tools
candidates.summary: GitHub changelog dated Nov 17, 2026: Copilot Evals is in public preview for Copilot Individual, Business and Enterprise plans. It lets users create repeatable evals for a skill, custom agent or MCP tool, and compare runs from before and after a customization change. Users approve each run before it starts.
candidates.audience_why: Developers building agent setups with skills and MCP tools need a way to check whether changes actually help; this is a concrete tool for that.
candidates.visual_angle: Self-made diagram of the eval loop: create eval, approve run, compare before/after. No imitation of GitHub UI.
candidates.hook: GitHub just added a way to test your Copilot skills and MCP tools like code.
cautions: Page says to install it in VS Code, Copilot CLI or the Copilot app; do not claim more surfaces.

sources.claim: Copilot Evals is in public preview for Copilot Individual, Business and Enterprise plans; an eval is a repeatable test for a skill, custom agent or MCP tool; compare runs before and after a customization change; you approve each run before it starts; installable in VS Code, Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app.

candidates.title: GPT-6.2 Astra vs Sol: which one for which job
candidates.summary: OpenAI API changelog entry dated Nov 17, 2026: use GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding reasoning and coding tasks, or GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding and agent workflows. The entry states tool calling requires the Responses API.
candidates.audience_why: Engineers choosing a model for coding agents need to know the split between the two variants and the API requirement for tool calling.
candidates.visual_angle: Two-column comparison card (Astra vs Sol) with the Responses API requirement shown as a flow arrow; no vendor logos.
candidates.hook: OpenAI split GPT-6.2 into two models, and tool calling needs the Responses API.
cautions: No benchmark claims are sourced; do not state which model is better beyond OpenAI's stated use cases.
Check pricing/availability on the model pages before scripting if mentioned.

sources.claim: Entry dated Nov 17: GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding reasoning and coding tasks, GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding and agent workflows; tool calling requires the Responses API.

candidates.title: Background completion windows: 30 to 40 percent cheaper tokens
candidates.summary: OpenAI API changelog entry dated Nov 17, 2026: developers can choose a two-hour or eight-hour background completion window in the Responses API public beta. Model token rates are 30% lower than Standard for the two-hour window and 40% lower for the eight-hour window.
candidates.audience_why: Developers running batch-style jobs can trade latency for lower cost; the trade-off is the useful takeaway.
candidates.visual_angle: Self-made bar chart of relative token rate: Standard 100, two-hour 70, eight-hour 60, labelled with source and date.
candidates.hook: If your AI job can wait two hours, OpenAI's API now charges less for it.
cautions: Public beta. Single changelog source; check Responses API docs before scripting.

sources.claim: Entry dated Nov 17: choose a two-hour or eight-hour background completion window in the Responses API public beta; model token rates 30% lower than Standard for two-hour and 40% lower for eight-hour.

candidates.title: GPT-Live-1.1 standby: voice sessions that pause when idle
candidates.summary: OpenAI API changelog entry dated Nov 19, 2026: GPT-Live-1.1 improves pronunciation, accent consistency and transcription in multilingual voice conversations. Standby for GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1 WebRTC sessions pauses inference during inactivity and resumes when someone speaks.
candidates.audience_why: Developers building voice agents care about idle cost and multilingual accuracy.
candidates.visual_angle: Self-made session timeline: speaking, silence triggers standby, speech resumes inference.
candidates.hook: A voice AI session can now pause its inference while nobody is talking.

sources.claim: Entry dated Nov 19: GPT-Live-1.1 improves pronunciation, accent consistency and transcription in multilingual voice conversations; standby for GPT-Live-1 and 1.1 WebRTC sessions pauses inference during inactivity and resumes when someone speaks.

candidates.title: Gemini 4 Neon arrives in GitHub Copilot
candidates.summary: GitHub changelog dated Nov 18, 2026: Gemini 4 Neon is generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users. Per Google, its quality is close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task. Rollout is gradual.
candidates.audience_why: Developers choosing a model in their IDE want to know what is on their plan and what the vendor claims about cost.
candidates.visual_angle: Self-made card listing plans and the vendor-stated comparison, clearly attributed.
candidates.hook: Gemini 4 Neon is now in GitHub Copilot, and Google says it costs less per task than Carbon.
cautions: Cost and quality comparison is vendor-stated; attribute to Google.

sources.claim: Gemini 4 Neon is generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users; per Google, quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at lower token cost per task; rollout is gradual.

candidates.title: OpenAI's free CSAM image classifier for approved organizations
candidates.summary: OpenAI API changelog entry dated Nov 16, 2026: approved organizations can use the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier at no cost to help prioritize images for human review. It returns separate signals for potential CSAM and potential AI-generated CSAM.
candidates.audience_why: Developers on trust and safety or platform teams may use such classifiers; focus on the human-review workflow.
candidates.visual_angle: Abstract flow diagram: queue, classifier signals, human review. No imagery of harmful content.
candidates.hook: OpenAI made a child-safety image classifier free for approved organizations.
cautions: Sensitive subject; keep strictly to what the entry states.

sources.claim: Entry dated Nov 16: approved organizations can use the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier at no cost to help prioritize images for human review; separate signals for potential CSAM and potential AI-generated CSAM.

candidates.title: MCP goes stateless: what changed in the 2026-07-28 spec
candidates.summary: MCP blog post dated Jul 28, 2026: MCP is moving from a bidirectional stateful protocol to a request/response stateless protocol. Any request can land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer. Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated but keep working for at least twelve months.
candidates.audience_why: Anyone building or hosting MCP servers needs to know why session handling and scaling assumptions changed.
candidates.visual_angle: Self-made before/after diagram: sticky stateful session vs stateless requests across a load balancer.
candidates.hook: MCP dropped its stateful session model, so any server instance can take any request.
cautions: Evergreen: published Jul 28, 2026, outside the news window; do not frame as new.

sources.claim: MCP is moving from a bidirectional stateful protocol to a request/response stateless protocol; any request can land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer; Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated but keep working for at least twelve months.
